question.leadin: A powerful family that ruled this city included men like Lorezno the Magnificent.
question.text: Name this Italian city once ruled by the Medici family. This city is the most populous one in Tuscany.
question.clue: After Turin and before Rome became capital, it was the capital of the Kingdom of Italy.

swap.leadin: This leader and his mistress Claretta Petacci were allegedly hung on meathooks.
swap.text: Name this former Socialist and fascist world leader. He was nicknamed "Il Duce" (eel doo-chay) and was supported by the paramilitary Blackshirts.
swap.clue: This man was the only leader of the Republic of Salo.

question.leadin: This leader is known as the "Hero of Two Worlds" for his leadership in the Ragamuffin War and the Uruguayan Civil War. --.
question.text: Name this leader of the Redshirts, who fought the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies during the Expedition of the Thousand in the Risorgimento.
question.clue: This man allied with Brazil and the Colorados during the Uruguayan Civil War, thus earning the nickname "Hero of Two Worlds."

swap.text: This prime minister of the Kingdom of Piedmont-Sardinia and founder of the newspaper Il Risorgimento became the first prime minister of the unified Kingdom of Italy.
swap.clue: This politician ceded Nice and Savoy to that other leader in exchange for assistance in a war that included the Battle of Solferino.

question.leadin: The League of Cambrai was formed in opposition to this city.
question.text: Name this city famed for its leaders known as doges [pronounced "doajes"] and its gondoliers, who travel along its many canals.
question.clue: This city-state's hinterland, the "Domini di Terraferma," was partitioned between Austria and the Cisalpine Republic by the provisions of the 1797 Treaty of Campo Formio.

swap.leadin: This city originally served as a refugee camp for citizens fleeing from Rome in the 5th century, despite being built on a marsh.
swap.text: Name this Northern Italian city that was its own independent republic from the 7th to 18th centuries. It rivaled the Ottoman Empire for power in the Mediterranean.
swap.answerHtml: Most Serene Republic of Venice [prompt on “Venetian Republic”]
swap.clue: This republic's leaders participated in the annual "Marriage of the Sea" ceremony using the ceremonial raft Bucentaur.

question.leadin: Many city-states in Italy grew very rich and prosperous after the 4th Crusade.
question.text: This city-state became an autonomous Duchy after the 1183 CE Peace of Constance. Today, this city is the capital of Lombardy and is the 2nd most populous Italian city.
question.clue: In 286 CE, Diocletian made it the capital of the Western Roman Empire.

swap.text: This grandfather of Lorenzo de Medici was a skillful statesman during the Italian Renaissance, doing things like keeping councillors in the Florentine Signoria loyal to him. He was succeeded by his son, Piero.
swap.clue: This man persuaded Pope Eugene IV to move the Council of Ferrara to his city, thereby attracting Byzantine wealth and learning.

question.text: Manius Valerius Maximus brought the first Roman sundial back from the city of Catania in this region. This region, a major source of grain for the Roman Republic, was the site of the first two Servile Wars.
question.clue: The Expedition of the Thousand targeted a kingdom named for two of this region, and this region's namesake "Vespers" revolted against France in the thirteenth century.

swap.text: After the Yugoslav partisans' victory, people of this ethnicity were targeted in the Foibe Massacres. The modern city of Dubrovnik was renamed after many members of this ethnic group left Istria and Dalmatia.
swap.clue: Many people of this ethnicity settled in the state of Rio Grande do Sul, which was supported by a leader of this ethnicity during the Ragamuffin War.

question.leadin: Name these inventors of the early 20th and late 19th century.
question.text: This Italian physicist, who won the 1909 Nobel Prize, extended the work of Heinrich Hertz and was one of the first people to transmit radio waves. He is known as the inventor of the radio.
question.clue: This man's first transmission was, "Are you ready," and at Toynbee Hall, he gave the lecture, "Telegraphy without Wires."

swap.leadin: This family fled to Venice after Piero the Gouty acceded to all the demands of Charles VIII.
swap.text: Name this Italian family led by men like Cosimo the Elder and Lorenzo the Magnificent.
swap.clue: People with this last name founded a Platonic Academy and were targeted in the Pazzi Conspiracy.

question.text: Supported by Charles Emmanuel III, Rosa Govone organized a convitti consisting of a series of shelters and textile shops to provide work to young women throughout this duchy. Monarchs of Italy following the 19th-century reunification came from a family named for this duchy's namesake county, who ruled Piedmont-Sardinia.
question.answerHtml: Duchy of Savoy [or Duché de Savoie or Ducato di Savoia; accept County of Savoy; accept House of Savoy or Savoyards]
question.clue: That duke of this region married his son to the sister of Louis XIII, Christine Marie.

swap.leadin: King Ferdinand IV created the title "Duke of Bronte" for Horatio Nelson after a naval blockade forced Jacobin troops in this city to surrender to Fabrizio Ruffo's Sanfedisti.
swap.text: Name this city whose poorest class, the Lazzaroni, rose up against the French-backed Parthenopean Republic. The Expedition of the Thousand captured this capital of the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies.
swap.clue: A tax on fruit prompted a fisherman to lead a rebellion in this city, in which Fabrizio Ruffio led the Papal Sanfedismo movement to overthrow the Napoleonic Parthenopean Republic.

question.text: The U.S. 10th Mountain Division was deployed at Riva Ridge at the Battle of Monte Castello in the winter of 1944, during General Clark's assault on this northernmost defensive fortification in Italy.
question.clue: Brazil's memorial honors members of the Brazilian Expeditionary Force killed trying to capture this Axis defensive position. Operation Olive partially broke through this line defended by Albert Kesselring in Italy's Apennine ("APP-uh-nine") Mountains.

swap.text: The Allied invasion of Sicily was given this canine-related codename. It culminated in Benito Mussolini being driven out of power.

question.text: Dante Alighieri argued against Boniface's position in his treatise De Monarchia, a position which aligned with him being a member of the White branch of this faction, which clashed in Italian politics with the Ghibellines.
question.clue: Charles of Anjou helped this group in establishing themselves in their most important city where the Donati and Cerchi families created "black" and "white" factions, Florence.

swap.text: The essay highlights the non-participation of Elisabetta, a duchess of this family, in activities in The Book of the Courtier over which she ostensibly presides. Isabella D'Este married into this ruling family of Mantua.

question.leadin: During this period, right-wing extremists founded the "New Order Scholarship Center", which was banned as a fascist group. FTPE.
question.text: Name this period of political instability, marked by the violence of paramilitary organizations such as the October 22 Group. This period is often said to run from the death of Antionio Annarumma in 1969 through to the Salerno Massacre in 1982.
question.clue: This period was preceded by a series of violent strikes known as the Hot Autumn.

swap.text: Zeno eventually came to see Odoacer as a major rival, causing him to offer Italy to this Ostrogothic ruler, who killed Odoacer during a banquet.
swap.clue: He won the original Battle of the Isonzo, which led to an amusing banquet in which he toasted - and then personally strangled - the man who had deposed Romulus Augustulus.
